s, a, t, i, p, n

curatorBrief.title: Letter Sounds: s, a, t, i, p, n
curatorBrief.intent: Welcome kindergarten learners to Group 1 letter sounds (s, a, t, i, p, n). Introduce the sounds /s/, /ă/, /t/, /ĭ/, /p/, /n/ with clear visual cues and emphasize clean articulation without adding 'uh' (schwa).

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Letter-Sound Group 1: s, a, t, i, p, n. Produce the correct, most common sound for each letter in the set when shown the grapheme (the letter shape).

components.title: Meet the Letters and Their Clean Sounds
components.intent: Introduce the letters s, a, t, i, p, n with clear pictures of everyday objects (snake, apple, turtle, igloo, pig, nest) and explain the importance of saying clean sounds like a crisp /t/ instead of 'tuh'.

components.title: Listen and Say the Sounds
components.intent: Guide students through interactive direct instruction where the tutor models continuous and vowel sounds (/s/, /ă/, /ĭ/, /n/), practices them together, and prompts the student to say the clean phoneme into the microphone.

components.title: Letter Shape Spotter
components.intent: Help kindergarteners recognize and discriminate the visual graphemes s, a, t, i, p, n in lowercase and uppercase forms before independent sound production.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Independently produce the most common sound for each letter in this cumulative set, when shown its grapheme: s, a, t, i, p, n.

components.title: Say the Sound for Each Letter
components.intent: Direct instruction where students are shown individual letter graphemes from Group 1 (s, a, t, i, p, n) and independently speak the corresponding clean sound aloud without teacher pre-cueing.

components.title: Sound Recall Match
components.intent: Provide untimed retrieval practice linking each letter grapheme (s, a, t, i, p, n) to its correct initial keyword sound picture to solidify automatic recall.

finalAssessment.title: Super Sound Check: s, a, t, i, p, n
finalAssessment.intent: Assess students across all 6 target letter-sound correspondences (s, a, t, i, p, n), prompting them to match letters to clean spoken phonemes and beginning sound pictures.

cards.title: Snake and Apple
cards.definition: Letter S hisses like snake, and A opens for apple.
cards.originStory: We draw a curvy snake to make the letter S shape.
cards.curiosityNote: Your tongue stays behind your teeth to hiss!
cards.visualPrompt: A friendly green snake curled in an S shape next to a shiny red apple with the letter a on it, bright cartoon style.

cards.title: Quick Turtle Tap
cards.definition: Letter T makes a tiny, quiet tap with your tongue.
cards.originStory: A tall turtle standing straight looks like letter T.
cards.curiosityNote: A quiet tap stops your breath instantly!
cards.visualPrompt: A cheerful little turtle tapping its foot beside a cozy snowy igloo, warm storybook art style.

cards.title: Pig and Nest
cards.definition: Pop your lips for pig, then hum for nest.
cards.originStory: Letters help us spell real words like pin and pan.
cards.curiosityNote: Hold your nose to feel letter N vibrate!
cards.visualPrompt: A cute pink pig peeking into a cozy twig nest with baby blue eggs, colorful children's book illustration.

problems.question: Which one starts with the same sound as sun?
problems.rationale: Snake begins with the hissing /s/ sound, just like the word sun. A turtle begins with the tapping /t/ sound, while an ant begins with the short /a/ sound. Matching snake with sun helps us hear and connect the same starting sound.
problems.teachingNote: Kindergarteners often confuse the sounds /s/ and /t/ because both are made with the tongue near the front teeth. Emphasize the continuous hissing sound of /s/ compared to the quick stop of /t/.
successCriteria: Identify the initial /s/ sound in spoken words
Distinguish the /s/ sound from the /t/ and /a/ initial sounds
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which one starts with the sound of letter p?
problems.rationale: The word pig begins with the /p/ sound, which is the sound made by the letter p. Nest begins with the /n/ sound, and sun begins with the /s/ sound.
problems.teachingNote: Prompt students to press their lips together to make the unvoiced /p/ sound without adding 'uh' (avoid saying 'puh'). Have them feel the gentle puff of air on their hand.
successCriteria: Identify the initial /p/ sound represented by the letter p
Distinguish the /p/ sound from other initial consonant sounds like /n/ and /s/
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which one starts with the /p/ sound?
problems.rationale: Pig begins with the popping /p/ sound like /p/-pig. Both ant and apple begin with the short /a/ vowel sound instead. Sorting by starting sounds helps us hear the very first sound a word makes.
problems.teachingNote: Have learners place their hands gently in front of their lips to feel the small puff of air made by /p/ compared to the open-mouth vowel sound /a/.
successCriteria: Isolate the initial phoneme in familiar CVC or short words
Distinguish between initial /p/ and initial /a/ sounds
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word starts with the /t/ sound?
problems.rationale: Tiger begins with the /t/ sound made by the letter T. Iguana begins with the /i/ sound, and nest starts with the /n/ sound.
problems.teachingNote: Encourage students to feel their tongue tap right behind their front teeth when making the quick, unvoiced /t/ sound.
successCriteria: Identify the initial /t/ sound in spoken words
Distinguish the /t/ sound from other Group 1 sounds like /i/ and /n/
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.statement: The letter 's' makes the /s/ sound like in the word sun.
problems.rationale: The letter 's' represents the crisp /s/ sound at the beginning of words like sun, snake, and sit. Recognizing this sound helps young readers blend letters together to read simple words.
problems.teachingNote: Reinforce the sound by having students make a gentle hissing sound like a snake when they see the letter 's'.
successCriteria: Identify the primary sound associated with the letter s
Connect letter-sounds to familiar everyday words
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word starts with the sound of the letter i?
problems.rationale: The letter i makes the short /ĭ/ sound heard at the beginning of insect. While ice cream starts with the letter's name, the primary phonics sound taught in this group is the short /ĭ/ sound. Apple begins with the /ă/ sound, which belongs to the letter a.
problems.teachingNote: Kindergarteners frequently confuse a letter's sound with its letter name. Remind students that the foundational sound for letter i is /ĭ/ as in insect or igloo, rather than the long sound /ī/ heard in ice cream.
successCriteria: Identify the short /ĭ/ sound for the letter i.
Distinguish the short vowel sound /ĭ/ from the long vowel sound /ī/.
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS
